findings.who: A filer divorced under a 2020 decree who in 2025 receives (or pays) fixed cash installments that the decree calls an equitable-distribution or equalization payment. The decree does not say the payments are not alimony, and they stop if the recipient dies.
findings.why_no: The help says 'a division of property are not alimony', and the payments are not 'support'. The filer answers no. Under former IRC section 71(b)(1), which NY adopts, a cash payment under a divorce instrument is alimony when it is not designated as non-alimony, the parties are not in the same household, and liability ends at death. How the parties label the payment does not matter.
findings.irs_text: ny_it225i p. 10, A-119: 'An applicable alimony or separate maintenance payment is a payment made under an alimony or separation instrument (as defined in IRC § 71 as it was in effect immediately prior to the enactment of Public Law 115-97) that was executed after December 31, 2018.'
findings.fix: Ask about facts the filer can check: 'Did you (or your spouse) pay or receive any cash payments to or for a spouse or former spouse under a divorce decree, court order or written separation agreement, including installments described as a property settlement?' Then classify only payments the instrument expressly calls not alimony, or that continue after the recipient's death, as outside the line.

findings.who: A filer paying a former spouse in 2025 under a 2021 written agreement signed incident to their divorce. Examples are a post-decree modification agreement or a stipulation the parties signed but did not have entered as a court order.
findings.why_no: The gate names only 'a court order or a written separation agreement'. The filer thinks of the document as a settlement or modification agreement, neither an order nor a 'separation agreement', and reads the list as complete.
findings.irs_text: ny_it225i p. 10, A-119: 'alimony or separation instrument (as defined in IRC § 71 as it was in effect immediately prior to the enactment of Public Law 115-97)', which includes a written instrument incident to a divorce decree.
findings.fix: Broaden the wording to 'under a divorce or separation decree, a court order, or any written agreement between you and the spouse or former spouse, including one signed at or after the divorce'.

locators: p. 10, A-119, "An applicable alimony or separate maintenance payment is a payment made under an alimony or separation instrument (as defined in IRC § 71 as it was in effect immediately prior to the enactment of Public Law 115-97) that was executed after December 31, 2018."; p. 18, S-136, "If you made any applicable alimony or separate maintenance payments during the tax year, then enter the amount paid."
p. 10, A-119, "If you received any applicable alimony or separate maintenance payments during the tax year, then enter the amount received."

findings.who: A full-year New York City resident with no business who, as a beneficiary, received an accumulation distribution from a trust in 2025. The trust had paid New York City tax on that income in earlier years. No Schedule C is on the return.
findings.why_no: The computed gate counts Schedules C. With none on the return, the gate is false, the question is never asked, and line 53 is set to zero.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 15, Line 53: "Can you claim the New York City unincorporated business tax (UBT) credit, the New York City accumulation distribution credit, or the part-year resident nonrefundable New York City child and dependent care credit? ... If Yes, complete Section C of Form IT-201-ATT and enter the amount from Form IT-201-ATT, line 10, on line 53."
findings.fix: Do not tie line 53 to Schedule C. Gate on New York City full-year or part-year residence (for either spouse), then ask each of the three credits separately, as the instructions do.

findings.who: A W-2 employee who moved into or out of New York City during 2025 and paid child care so they could work. No Schedule C is on the return.
findings.why_no: The Schedule C gate is false, so the part-year resident New York City child and dependent care credit is never reached and line 53 is zero.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 15, Line 53: "...or the part-year resident nonrefundable New York City child and dependent care credit?"
findings.fix: Gate on part-year New York City residence. Ask: "Were you (or your spouse) a New York City resident for only part of 2025 and did you pay child or dependent care expenses?"

findings.who: A New York City resident who is a partner in a partnership, such as a law or medical partnership, or an LLC member. The partnership paid New York City UBT for 2025. The filer reports the income on Schedule E (K-1), and neither spouse has a Schedule C.
findings.why_no: No Schedule C means the gate is false. The UBT credit available to resident partners for their share of partnership UBT is dropped.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 15, Line 53: "Can you claim the New York City unincorporated business tax (UBT) credit..." (the instructions do not limit the credit to sole proprietors)
findings.fix: Ask whether any business owned by you or your spouse, alone or through a partnership or LLC, paid New York City UBT. Do not condition the question on Schedule C.

findings.who: A New York City resident sole proprietor (has a Schedule C) whose business owes no UBT, for example because it is below the filing threshold. The same filer received a trust accumulation distribution, or was a part-year New York City resident with child care costs.
findings.why_no: The gated question asks only "Did your ... business pay New York City unincorporated business tax for 2025?" The truthful answer is no, and the other two credits on the same line are never asked.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 15, Line 53: "...the New York City accumulation distribution credit, or the part-year resident nonrefundable New York City child and dependent care credit?"
findings.fix: Use the instructions' full question listing all three credits, or ask three separate yes/no questions.

findings.who: A New York City resident partner whose own Schedule C covers an unrelated side business. The partnership, not the filer's Schedule C business, paid UBT.
findings.why_no: "Did your ... business pay" reads as the Schedule C business the gate just keyed on. The partnership paid the UBT, not 'my business'.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 15, Line 53: "Can you claim the New York City unincorporated business tax (UBT) credit..."
findings.fix: Say "any business you or your spouse own or are a partner or LLC member in, including through a partnership".

findings.who: A sole proprietor whose business uses a fiscal year ending in 2025. Alternatively, a sole proprietor whose 2025 UBT is owed but not yet paid, or was paid in 2026 with the NYC-202.
findings.why_no: "pay ... for 2025" reads as a payment made in calendar 2025 for calendar 2025. A fiscal-year filer, or one who has not yet paid, answers no.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 15: "you may also be required to file New York City's Form NYC-202, Unincorporated Business Tax Return for Individuals and Single-Member LLCs"; Line 53 "Can you claim the New York City unincorporated business tax (UBT) credit"
findings.fix: Ask: "Is UBT owed or paid (Form NYC-202 or NYC-202S, or a partnership's NYC-204) for a business tax year ending in 2025?"

findings.who: A Schedule C filer who paid UBT and reads the help text.
findings.why_no: "which this tool does not compute" suggests the answer has no effect or the credit is unavailable here, inviting a no.
findings.irs_text: ny_it201i p. 15, Line 53: "If Yes, complete Section C of Form IT-201-ATT and enter the amount from Form IT-201-ATT, line 10, on line 53."
findings.fix: Say that a yes requires completing Form IT-201-ATT Section C, and prompt the filer for the line 10 amount.

locators: Schedule 1 (2025), line 3, "Business income or (loss). Attach Schedule C"
